findings.title: Start/stop oracle turns undated historical correlations into current actionable advice
findings.what: StartStopRow has no observation timestamp or dataset cutoff, evidenceRefs omit a date, and the summary says traits “historically end badly” before advising users to treat new matching openers as a don't-start/stop-early signal. Consumers cannot tell when the evidence was current, so stale historical behavior is presented as present guidance rather than “as of <date>.”
findings.fix: Carry an evidence cutoff date into the audit input or derive it from timestamped rows, then include `as-of:<YYYY-MM-DD>` in evidenceRefs and phrase the summary and fallback rationale as “As of <date> …”. Suppress the finding when a trustworthy cutoff cannot be established.
findings.acceptance: A deterministic test supplies dated rows and verifies the finding includes an exact `as-of:YYYY-MM-DD` evidence reference and matching “As of YYYY-MM-DD” summary text; an undated dataset must not emit current-tense actionable advice.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read the row schema and complete emission path at baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. The only row fields are sessionId, project, opener, and good; neither the aggregate evidence references nor summary/rationale contains a date or cutoff. The claim therefore survives as a concrete stale-signal provenance defect.
